_readme: Phase 2 codemod input for the Color Consistency Directive migration.

Scope: exact-match, case-insensitive hex swaps only — every entry here is a hex value that is IDENTICAL to a light-mode --cc-* token in index.css, so swapping it for var(--cc-*) is lossless with zero ambiguity.

NOT included: Tailwind palette utility classes (text-blue-600, bg-emerald-500/10, etc). Those don't have a single correct --cc-* target without knowing the author's intent per call site (status? brand accent? arbitrary?) — that's Phase 3 manual triage, not a safe mechanical swap.

NOT included: near-match hex values that are close-but-not-identical to a --cc-* token (e.g. #E8457B vs #E8457A) — those are almost always someone's hand-typed approximation and deserve a human glance, not a silent swap to a slightly different shade.

Dark-mode note: --cc-* tokens have separate values under .dark in index.css, resolved automatically at paint time via the CSS custom property. Swapping a literal light-mode hex for var(--cc-plum) makes that value dark-mode-aware for free — this IS the actual bug being fixed (hardcoded hex never adapted to dark mode; the var reference now will).

Recommended codemod behavior: for each hexToVar entry, replace exact string matches of the hex (case-insensitive, both #rrggbb forms) found inside style={{ color: '...' }} / style={{ background: '...' }} object literals and inside Tailwind arbitrary-value classes like text-[#E8457A] / bg-[#E8457A] with the corresponding cssVar. Do not touch hex values inside comments, non-color contexts (e.g. a hex-looking string in unrelated data), or index.css itself (already the source of truth).

#E8457A.name: CareCliQ Pink — primary actions, active states

#FFFBEB.name: Amber tint background (also matches --cc-status-warning-bg — check surrounding context to pick the right one)

#F0F9FF.name: Sky tint background (also matches --cc-status-info-bg — check context)

#FFFFFF.name: Card/panel surface — CAUTION: #FFFFFF is also used deliberately as literal white text-on-color in many places (e.g. white text on a plum button). Only swap when it's clearly a card/page background, not a foreground/text colour.

#F5EFFE.name: Alert pill background (also matches --cc-status-critical-bg — check context)

#7C3AED.name: Status/destructive-action: brand purple (NOT the same concept as danger/red below — see index.css comment: 'pink = brand/action, red = danger, users must never confuse the two')

#EF4444.name: Status: real danger/safety-critical severity — deliberately distinct from --cc-status-critical (see above)

tailwindPaletteClassesNotMigrated._note: These showed up hundreds of times in the audit (text-blue-600, bg-emerald-500/10, text-rose-500, bg-slate-400, etc). Each one needs a human decision about which --cc-* concept it's actually standing in for at that call site — status color? brand accent? pure decoration? There is no single correct global answer, so Phase 2 should skip these entirely and leave them for Phase 3's manual triage of the worst-offending files.

commonIntentMapping (for a human doing P.red-*/rose-*: check intent carefully: real danger/safety severity → var(--cc-status-danger); a brand-styled destructive ACTION (delete button etc) → var(--cc-status-critical), which is purple, not red, in this design system
commonIntentMapping (for a human doing P.slate-*/gray-*: usually meant a neutral → var(--cc-muted) (text) or var(--cc-border) (borders/dividers)
commonIntentMapping (for a human doing P.sky-*/indigo-*/violet-*/purple-*: check whether it's standing in for the brand accent → var(--cc-coral), or informational → var(--cc-status-info)
